title: Reformed grant illuminated yet vicious assent — but refuse true/saving name (James)
source_text: XXXII. Agnoscunt tamen non solum humanam quandam fidem & persuasionem Dei Verbo & Doctrinae Christianae adhiberi posse, ab iis qui perdite & flagitiose vivunt, & dilectione Dei destituuntur; sed etiam multos esse quorum Spiritus Sanctus mentes illuminavit, ut verbi divini veritatem agnoscant, & theoretice illi assentientur, qui nihilominus vitiis indulgent, nec Deum syncere diligunt. Sed quanquam tales in Scriptura saepius credere dicantur, & Dei Verbum quandam illis fidei speciem tribuat, illam tamen fidem veram & salvificam dici nolunt; quoniam, juxta ipsos, illa sola fides verae & salvificae titulum meretur, quae justitiam & salutem homini actu confert, quod praestare non potest modo descripta fides. Nam ad salutem homini, teste Jacobo, nihil prodest. Et propterea quanquam a Spiritu Sancto procedat, & assensum non omnino fictum veritati divinae praebeat, illam tamen simpliciter & absolute veram dici nolunt: sed historicae nomine eam distinguere solent a fide viva atque salvifica, cui nomen verae fidei appropriant. Ac proinde quod dicunt veram fidem esse penitus a charitate inseparabilem, ex eorum mente intelligendum est, de fide viva atque efficaci, quae sola ad salutem prodest, & hominem actu justificare valet.
pass_a_gloss: Yet they acknowledge not only that a certain human faith and persuasion can be given to God's Word and Christian doctrine by those who live ruinously and shamefully and lack love of God; but also that there are many whose minds the Holy Spirit has illuminated so that they acknowledge the truth of the divine word and assent to it theoretically, who nevertheless indulge vices and do not sincerely love God. But although such are often said in Scripture to believe, and God's Word attributes to them a certain appearance of faith, they nevertheless refuse to have that faith called true and saving; because, according to them, only that faith deserves the title of true and saving which actually confers righteousness and salvation on a man — which the faith just described cannot do. For it profits a man nothing for salvation, as James testifies. And therefore although it proceeds from the Holy Spirit and gives an assent to divine truth not altogether feigned, they still refuse to call it simply and absolutely true: but usually distinguish it by the name historic from living and saving faith, to which they appropriate the name of true faith. And therefore when they say true faith is utterly inseparable from charity, it is to be understood on their mind of living and efficacious faith, which alone profits for salvation and can actually justify a man.
pass_b_english: Reformed grant Spirit-lit theoretical assent in the vicious — yet deny it the true/saving name.
James: such faith does not save; 'true' is reserved for living efficacious faith inseparable from charity (James 2).
